title: Four-Way Pileup: Team Pillbert Topples the HULK as Underdogs Sweep Week 4
dek: Alan's 29% long shot knocks off No Banner only HULK, Zoe and Kaushal pull upsets of their own, and the league wakes up with four teams tied at 3-1.
body: The undefeated era lasted exactly three weeks. Alan's Team Pillbert beat Ramon's No Banner only HULK 125.42 to 116.72 as a 29% underdog, handing the league's juggernaut its first loss. The difference-maker was a brand-new arrival: Javonte Williams, freshly acquired from Randy, posted 28.8 points on a 13.25 projection in his Team Pillbert debut. Even scarier for the rest of the league, Kyle Monangai scored 27.5 on Alan's bench against a 7.57 projection, so the upset could have been a rout. Philly's title odds more than doubled, from 9% to 21%, and the bad guy is now the second favorite in the building.

Ramon didn't get beaten so much as out-swung. Kenneth Walker III gave the HULK 30.4 points on an 18.89 projection, and the team still leads the league with 561 points, a full 80.1 ahead of anyone else. But the title odds dropped from 52% to 41%, and for the first time this season No Banner only HULK is sharing the top line of the standings instead of owning it. Brucie spent the week doing kicker housekeeping, picking up Jason Myers, whom Alan had just cut, and dropping Cameron Dicker, plus adding the Bills D/ST. Somewhere a controller is bracing for impact.

The other upset of the week belonged to the rookie. Zoe's Ghostu-Spider SZN beat Sonny's The Horse is Hea 120.88 to 95.1 as a 30% underdog, led by Tetairoa McMillan's 38.2 points on a 13.5 projection, the best line in the league. Bijan Robinson added 27.2, and Nico Collins scored 27.3 on her bench, which means Zilgit beat the defending champion by nearly 26 while leaving a WR1 day unused. For Sonny, it was a rough debut for his trade: Chuba Hubbard scored 25.4 on the bench while Parker Washington posted 1.5 on a 12.79 projection. Even the perfect swap would have left the commish 1.88 points short, which is the kind of math that makes a loss sting in two directions.

Kaushal finally got his first win, and he got it loudly. Habibsters hammered Randy's The fumblers 140.1 to 96.88 as a 39% underdog, the top score of the week and a 43.22-point margin. CeeDee Lamb went for 32.8 on a 13.65 projection, and Habib now has 459.1 points, more than 3-1 The fumblers, which tells you how much of that 0-3 start was bad luck. His title odds jumped from 1% to 8%. Randy's side of the trade didn't help: Stefon Diggs scored 6 in his fumblers debut, on the same day Williams carried Alan past the HULK.

In the battle of winless teams, Mekhi's Dawgs beat Jordan's Counting or not Counting GV 107.54 to 90.22. Kyren Williams scored 31.7 on an 11.88 projection, which was enough to survive Ja'Marr Chase's 4.2 on a 16.54 projection. Jordan's Garrett Wilson matched that exact 4.2 dud against a 13.23 projection, and Counting or not Counting GV fell to 0-4 with 349.2 points and playoff odds that now read 0%. JMoney was busy anyway, adding Kirk Cousins for Marvin Harrison Jr., Dalton Schultz for Michael Pittman Jr., and Michael Wilson for Tank Bigsby.

The standings are now a logjam: No Banner only HULK, Team Pillbert, The Horse is Hea, and The fumblers are all 3-1, with title odds of 41%, 21%, 11%, and 14%. Ghostu-Spider SZN sits alone at 2-2 with 18% playoff odds, while Habibsters (38%) and Dawgs (22%) are 1-3 but very much breathing. The weekly busiest-manager award goes to Alan, who dropped De'Von Achane outright, added Ollie Gordon II, Tyreek Hill, and Kalif Raymond, swapped kicker Jason Myers for Spencer Shrader, cut Bryce Young, and then made two more trades: Isaiah Likely, Emeka Egbuka, and Denzel Boston to Jordan for Ashton Jeanty, and Davante Adams plus Jeanty to Mekhi for Justin Jefferson. Jeanty's stay in Team Pillbert colors was less a tenure than a layover.

The rest of the wire was lively too. Randy, of all people, went shopping, adding Trevor Lawrence for Justin Herbert, Darren Waller in place of Hunter Henry, and Jordan Addison. Sonny grabbed Tony Pollard for J.K. Dobbins, cut Mark Andrews, added Juwan Johnson, picked up the Bryce Young that Alan dropped, and swapped the Eagles D/ST for the Bears D/ST. Kaushal flipped Drake Maye for Sam Darnold, Kyle Pitts Sr. for Braelon Allen, and the 49ers D/ST for the Vikings D/ST, and added Keenan Allen, while Zoe swapped Kyler Murray for Jared Goff.

Week 5 is loaded. Dawgs host Team Pillbert, which means Mekhi gets to line up Davante Adams and Ashton Jeanty against the guy who just shipped them to him, a revenge game delivered by trade. The HULK and The fumblers meet in a 3-1 versus 3-1 showdown that will thin the top of the table, and Habibsters, fresh off the week's best score, take on the commissioner. Counting or not Counting GV faces Ghostu-Spider SZN, with Jordan hunting a first win and Zoe hunting her first winning record.

social.author: Pillbert Nation
social.text: Javonte Williams, one game in our colors: 28.8 points. The HULK, one game against us: first loss. Title odds 9% to 21%. Thank you, Randy. Sincerely.

social.author: HULK Smash Club
social.text: 561 points. Still first in scoring by 80. One loss does not a collapse make. Fumblers, you are next and we are cranky.

social.author: Spider SZN Hive
social.text: McMillan 38.2 on a 13.5 projection. Bijan 27.2. Nico Collins dropped 27.3 on our BENCH and we still beat the champ by 25.78. The rookie is not a rookie anymore.

social.author: Waiver Wire Wally
social.text: Alan this week: cut Achane, cut Bryce Young, cut Myers, added Hill, Gordon, Raymond, Shrader, traded for Jeanty, traded away Jeanty, got Jefferson. Man treats the transaction log like a group chat.

social.author: Habib Hive
social.text: 140.1. Top score in the league. CeeDee 32.8. We are 1-3 with more points than a 3-1 team. The two-time champ has entered the chat.

social.author: The Fantasy Insider
social.text: Sources confirm Chuba Hubbard scored 25.4 on Sonny's bench in his debut. Sources also confirm Parker Washington started and scored 1.5. Sources are wincing.

social.author: Dawgs Den
social.text: Kyren 31.7 covered for Chase 4.2. First W is in. Next week Adams and Jeanty face the guy who traded them. We did not schedule this. We are grateful anyway.

social.author: Midwest Mike
social.text: Four teams at 3-1. One team at 0-4. Counting or not Counting GV picked up Cousins, Schultz, and Michael Wilson. The rebuild is counting. The standings are not.

social.author: Fumblers Faithful
social.text: Diggs 6. Javonte 28.8 for the other guy. Lost by 43. Added Lawrence, Waller, and Addison. We are still 3-1 and we will not be taking questions.

trade_watch.take: The model already liked this one for Alan, and Week 4 made it look worse for Randy: Javonte Williams put up 28.8 in Team Pillbert's upset of the HULK while Stefon Diggs managed 6 for The fumblers. One week in, it's a 22.8-point gap and Alan is pulling away.

Sonny won the paper argument with Hubbard's bigger numbers, then left his 25.4 points on the bench in a loss to Zoe. Rashee Rice gave the HULK nothing and didn't start, so after one week both sides have exactly zero lineup points to show for it.

bios.1: The defending champs are 3-1, but a loss to Ghostu-Spider SZN with Chuba Hubbard's 25.4 on the bench halved title odds from 21% to 11%. Sonny reworked the roster with Tony Pollard, Juwan Johnson, and Bryce Young and gets a revitalized Habibsters next.
bios.2: Randy is 3-1 with 72% playoff odds, but a 43-point beatdown from Habibsters and a 6-point Diggs debut took the shine off. He has suddenly become active, adding Trevor Lawrence, Darren Waller, and Jordan Addison ahead of a showdown with the HULK.
bios.3: Jordan is 0-4 with a league-low 349.2 points and playoff odds that have hit 0%. He's churning the roster with Kirk Cousins, Dalton Schultz, Michael Wilson, and a three-player haul for Ashton Jeanty, and he gets Ghostu-Spider SZN next.
bios.4: Alan pulled off a 29% upset of the HULK on the back of new arrival Javonte Williams and then rebuilt half the roster, landing Justin Jefferson and cutting De'Von Achane. Three straight wins and title odds of 21% make Team Pillbert the league's hottest team.
bios.5: Kyren Williams' 31.7 got Mekhi his first win despite a 4.2 from Ja'Marr Chase. A new trade brought in Davante Adams and Ashton Jeanty, and the first test is against the team that sent them.
bios.6: Kaushal finally broke through with the week's top score, 140.1, and his 459.1 points outpace a 3-1 team. At 1-3 with title odds jumping from 1% to 8%, the two-time champ looks a lot more dangerous than his record.
bios.7: Still the league's scoring machine at 561 points, but the first loss knocked title odds from 52% to 41% and put Ramon in a four-way tie at 3-1. Playoff odds remain 97%; the question now is whether anyone can stay with him for a full season.
bios.8: Zoe's crew took down the defending champion behind Tetairoa McMillan's league-best 38.2 and now sits at 2-2. Playoff odds are only 18%, but with Bijan rolling and Nico Collins producing even from the bench, this team is trending up.
